statement: Whether the LD 350-1 mandible’s mix of primitive (Australopithecus-like) and derived (Homo-like) traits justifies genus-level (Homo) assignment from a single mandible and dentition was formally disputed in the scientific literature.
scholarly_disagreement: Whether one mandible/dentition with a mix of primitive and derived traits is sufficient to assign genus-level (Homo) status, versus requiring more complete cranial or postcranial material.

sources.citation: Comment on "Early Homo at 2.8 Ma..." Science, doi:10.1126/science.aab0591
Villmoare et al., reply to Comment. Science, doi:10.1126/science.aab1122

interpretations.position: The mandibular and dental morphology justifies assignment to Homo
interpretations.strongest_case: The derived, thinned symphyseal and dental proportions fall outside the Australopithecus afarensis range and align with later Homo.

interpretations.position: Genus-level assignment from a single mandible/dentition is not adequately supported

interpretations.strongest_case: Dental and mandibular traits alone have historically been unreliable for genus-level hominin taxonomy without cranial or postcranial confirmation.
